questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Duke Law School’s strong academic reputation, its high-quality academic environment, and the opportunity to gain educational and cultural experience in the United States.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.answer: Very easy. The team at Duke provided clear guidance and made the process straightforward.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance was needed.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find off-campus housing, although it was somewhat expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Some housing options are a bit far from the university, and public transportation is limited. It’s also important to consider the distance to grocery stores.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was very easy. Oleg and the team at Duke provided clear instructions and frequent follow-up emails, making it hard to miss any steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were presentations on some of the courses, most syllabi were available online, and it was possible to contact professors directly to discuss a specific course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I had no problems registering for the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If there are specific courses you prefer, register for them early before they fill up. This is explained clearly during orientation, and it was not a problem for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The exams may be slightly easier than in Denmark, but most courses require active participation and involve cold calling, which we do not have in Denmark. It is better than it sounds and encourages engagement. The difficulty of a course can vary depending on the professor, so that is worth considering. Almost all courses also have a fixed grade median of 3.5.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching at Duke Law is more demanding in terms of preparation and participation. Unlike at UCPH, where it is possible to attend seminars without having prepared and catch up later, students are expected to have completed the readings in advance due to active participation and cold calling. The professors are also more engaged with students and are generally excellent teachers who really know their subject matter—often to a higher degree than what I have experienced in Denmark. They actively encourage one-on-one meetings with students, which is not common at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the courses I took. Business Associations with Professor Bishop is a bit tougher than the others, but it is very well taught and provides a strong learning experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food and groceries were significantly more expensive than in Denmark, especially if you do not want to rely on fast food. There is also a lack of public transportation, which meant spending quite a lot on Ubers.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a great gym with excellent athletic facilities, as well as many social activities such as weekly bar reviews and other student-organized events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend attending the weekly bar review, as it is a great way to socialize, meet other students, and get to know the law school community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on road trips, as they are a great way to explore more of the U.S. and make the most of weekends and holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust. Being part of an LLM cohort with other international students meant that everyone was in a similar situation, which made the transition smooth.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be harder to socialize with local students, as many American J.D. students tend to spend most of their time with each other. However, having an open mind, being proactive, and making an effort to socialize helps, and it will be fine over time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans’ tendency to engage in frequent small talk, which takes some getting used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of people and how welcoming and friendly they were.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared for a participation-based teaching style with required readings and cold calling.
2. Register early for any courses you are particularly interested in.
3. Be social and say yes to activities—make an effort to have fun and engage with the experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know the other students in the LLM groups, as well as some American students, and building meaningful connections.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Initially, my English skills were a challenge when I first started at Duke, but they improved significantly over time. If English is holding you back, it should not discourage you—many international students are not fully fluent at the beginning either.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
